column1: Some of the most remarkable beetles are the dung beetles, which spend almost their whole lives eating and breeding in dung.
column2: 一些最非凡的甲虫是粪甲虫，它们几乎一生都在粪便中进食和繁殖。

column1: More than 4,000 species of these remarkable creatures have evolved and adapted to the world’s different climates and the dung of its many animals.
column2: 这些奇特生物已演化出超过4000个物种，并适应了世界各地不同的气候以及众多动物的粪便环境。

column1: Australia’s native dung beetles are scrub and woodland dwellers, specialising in coarse marsupial droppings and avoiding the soft cattle dung in which bush flies and buffalo flies breed.
column2: 澳大利亚原生的粪甲虫生活在灌木和林地，专门以有袋类动物的粗粪为食，避开那些适合苍蝇和水牛蝇繁殖的柔软牛粪。

column1: In the early 1960s George Bornemissza, then a scientist at the Australian Government’s premier research organisation, the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO), suggested that dung beetles should be introduced to Australia to control dung-breeding flies.
column2: 在20世纪60年代初，时任澳大利亚政府顶尖科研机构——联邦科学与工业研究组织（CSIRO）的科学家乔治·博内米斯扎提出，应将蜣螂引入澳大利亚，以控制牛粪繁殖的苍蝇。

column1: Between 1968 and 1982, the CSIRO imported insects from about 50 different species of dung beetle, from Asia, Europe and Africa, aiming to match them to different climatic zones in Australia.
column2: 在1968年至1982年间，澳大利亚联邦科学与工业研究组织从亚洲、欧洲和非洲的约50种粪金龟子中引进了昆虫，旨在将它们匹配到澳大利亚不同的气候区。

column1: Of the 26 species that are known to have become successfully integrated into the local environment, only one, an African species released in northern Australia, has reached its natural boundary.
column2: 在已知能够成功融入当地环境的26个物种中，仅有一种非洲物种被释放到澳大利亚北部，并抵达了其自然边界。

column1: Introducing dung beetles into a pasture is a simple process: approximately 1,500 beetles are released; a handful at a time, into fresh cow pats in the cow pasture.
column2: 将蜣螂引入牧场是一个简单的过程：大约1500只蜣螂被分批释放到牧场中新鲜的牛粪里。

column1: The beetles immediately disappear beneath the pats digging and tunnelling and, if they successfully adapt to their new environment, soon become a permanent, self-sustaining part of the local ecology.
column2: 这些甲虫会立刻钻入牛粪之下开始挖掘和隧道作业，如果成功适应新环境，很快就会成为当地生态系统中稳定且自我维持的一部分。

column1: In time they multiply and within three or four years the benefits to the pasture are obvious.
column2: 随着时间推移，它们会繁殖，三到四年内就能明显看到对牧场的好处。

column1: Dung beetles work from the inside of the pat so they are sheltered from predators such as birds and foxes.
column2: 蜣螂在粪团内部活动，因此能避开鸟类和狐狸等捕食者。

column1: Most species burrow into the soil and bury dung in tunnels directly underneath the pats, which are hollowed out from within.
column2: 大多数物种会在土壤中挖掘隧道，并将粪便埋藏在隧道底部——这些隧道是从粪堆内部挖出的空腔。

column1: Some large species originating from France excavate tunnels to a depth of approximately 30 cm below the dung pat.
column2: 一些来自法国的大型物种会挖掘深度约为30厘米的隧道，位于粪堆之下。

column1: These beetles make sausage-shaped brood chambers along the tunnels.
column2: 这些甲虫在隧道里建造香肠状的育幼室。

column1: The shallowest tunnels belong to a much smaller Spanish species that buries dung in chambers that hang like fruit from the branches of a pear tree.
column2: 那些最浅的隧道属于一种体型较小的西班牙物种所建造的，它们将粪便埋藏在像梨树枝头悬挂的果实一样垂下的房间中。

column1: South African beetles dig narrow tunnels of approximately 20 cm below the surface of the pat.
column2: 南非的甲虫会在地面下约20厘米处挖掘狭窄的隧道。

column1: Some surface-dwelling beetles, including a South African species, cut perfectly-shaped balls from the pat, which are rolled away and attached to the bases of plants.
column2: 一些生活在地表的甲虫，包括一种南非物种，会从泥土表面削出完美球形的球体，将其滚离并附着在植物基部。

column1: For maximum dung burial in spring, summer and autumn, farmers require a variety of species with overlapping periods of activity.
column2: 为了在春季、夏季和秋季实现最大程度的粪便埋藏，农民需要多种活动期重叠的物种。

column1: In the cooler environments of the state of Victoria, the large French species (2.5 cms long) is matched with smaller (half this size), temperate-climate Spanish species.
column2: 在维多利亚州的凉爽环境中，体型较大的法国物种（长2.5厘米）与体型较小、来自温带气候的西班牙物种相匹配。

column1: The former are slow to recover from the winter cold and produce only one or two generations of offspring from late spring until autumn.
column2: 前者恢复缓慢，从晚春到秋季只能产生一至两代后代。

column1: The latter, which multiply rapidly in early spring, produce two to five generations annually.
column2: 后者在早春迅速繁殖，每年可产生两到五代。

column1: The South African ball-rolling species, being a subtropical beetle, prefers the climate of northern and coastal New South Wales where it commonly works with the South African tunnelling species.
column2: 南非球滚甲虫属于亚热带物种，偏好新南威尔士州北部和沿海地区的气候环境，通常与南非掘洞甲虫共同出现。

column1: In warmer climates, many species are active for longer periods of the year.
column2: 在更温暖的气候中，许多物种的活跃期会持续更长时间。

column1: Dung beetles were initially introduced in the late 1960s with a view to controlling buffalo flies by removing the dung within a day or two and so preventing flies from breeding.
column2: 这些蜣螂是在20世纪60年代末被引入的，目的是通过在一两天内清除粪便来抑制水牛蝇的繁殖。

column1: However, other benefits have become evident.
column2: 然而，其他一些好处也已经显现出来。

column1: Once the beetle larvae have finished pupation, the residue is a first-rate source of fertiliser.
column2: 甲虫幼虫完成蛹化后，其残留物成为优质的肥料来源。

column1: The tunnels abandoned by the beetles provide excellent aeration and water channels for root systems.
column2: 甲虫废弃的隧道为根系提供了优良的通气和水流通道。

column1: In addition, when the new generation of beetles has left the nest the abandoned burrows are an attractive habitat for soil-enriching earthworms.
column2: 此外，当新一代甲虫离开巢穴后，被遗弃的洞穴成为土壤改良蚯蚓的理想栖息地。

column1: The digested dung in these burrows is an excellent food supply for the earthworms, which decompose it further to provide essential soil nutrients.
column2: 这些洞穴中的消化粪便为蚯蚓提供了优良的食料，蚯蚓进一步分解它，以供给土壤中必需的营养物。

column1: If it were not for the dung beetle, chemical fertiliser and dung would be washed by rain into streams and rivers before it could be absorbed into the hard earth, polluting water courses and causing blooms of blue-green algae.
column2: 如果没有蜣螂，化学肥料和粪便就会被雨水冲刷进溪流和河流，无法被土壤吸收，污染水体并引发蓝绿藻爆发。

column1: Without the beetles to dispose of the dung, cow pats would litter pastures making grass inedible to cattle and depriving the soil of sunlight.
column2: 如果没有甲虫来处理牛粪，牛粪就会散落在牧场，使草变得无法被牛食用，同时使土壤失去阳光照射。

column1: Australia’s 30 million cattle each produce 10-12 cow pats a day.
column2: 澳大利亚的3000万头牛每天每头产生10到12次牛粪。

column1: This amounts to 1.7 billion tonnes a year, enough to smother about 110,000 sq km of pasture, half the area of Victoria.
column2: 这相当于每年17亿吨，足以覆盖约11万平方公里的牧场，相当于维多利亚州面积的一半。

column1: Dung beetles have become an integral part of the successful management of dairy farms in Australia over the past few decades.
column2: 在过去的几十年里，蜣螂已成为澳大利亚奶牛场成功管理中不可或缺的一部分。

column1: A number of species are available from the CSIRO or through a small number of private breeders, most of whom were entomologists with the CSIRO’s dung beetle unit who have taken their specialised knowledge of the insect and opened small businesses in direct competition with their former employer.
column2: 有几种蜣螂可以从澳大利亚联邦科学与工业研究组织或少数私人繁育者那里获得。这些繁育者大多曾是该组织蜣螂研究组的昆虫学家，后来利用自己的专业知识开办小企业，直接与原来的雇主竞争。
